chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hijjal, from Nasr al-Attar, from the one he linked it up through a chain of narrators, saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): 'I swear that there are three things that are true: You and the Trustees after you are the Knowers (Urafa) through whom God is known; You are the Knowers through whom Paradise is entered only by those who know you and you know them; You are the Knowers through whom Hell is entered only by those who deny you and you deny them.'

key_terms.أَنْكَرَكُمْ: You denied them, referring to the Imams' rejection of those who deny them
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: The Trustees/Successors, referring to the Imams after Ali
key_terms.عُرَفَاءُ: The Knowers, those who possess deep knowledge of God and through whom He is known
key_terms.مَعْرِفَتِكُمْ: Your knowledge/recognition, referring to the spiritual and theological knowledge of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imams being called 'Urafa' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes the Imams as the epistemological keys to divine recognition, a concept central to Shia gnosis (Ma'rifah). It underscores the theological principle that salvation is inextricably linked to the acceptance of the Prophet's progeny, reflecting the Shia view that their authority is not merely political but essential for the validity of faith and entry into Paradise.
